texts.preamble: Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 1 In The Court Of Sh H S Sharma District Judge/Asj New Delhi Unique Id No.02403R0089342011 Crl. Appeal No. 17/2011 Pawan Goyal S/o Sh Babu Ram R/o H. No. 43, 100 Road Chawla Colony, Ballabhgarh Haryana. ............ Appellant Versus The State ( D.A.) ............. Respondent Date of institution of the appeal : 13.12.2011 Date of receipt of appeal in this court : 14.12.2011 Date of hearing arguments : 05.03.2012 Date of announcement of order : 28.03.2012 Present: Ms. Asha Tiwari and Sh M L Narang, Advocates for the appellant. Sh Om Parkash, Chief Public Prosecutor for respondent. Judgment (Oral):
texts.facts: This particular finding is to be given weight as against the variance pointed out by ld. Counsel for the appellant. It has been submitted that the adulteration is not due to the variations noticed by the two experts. 26 Since Kashi Nath's judgement (supra) is based on Bishan Sarup's judgement (supra) rendered by the Full Bench of the Hon'ble 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) High Court, decided on 19/9/2005 therefore, let me mention the facts of these two cases and the observations made by the Hon'ble High Court in these cases. 27 In Bishan Sarup 's case (supra) a sample of cow's milk was taken on 27/3/1962. On analysis by the Public Analyst vide his report dated 31/3/1962 the fat contents were found to be 6.7% and the non fatty solids were found to be 8.03% as against the prescribed standard of 8.5%. Since the non fatty solids were found to be deficient, therefore, the milk was declared to be adulterated. I need not touch the defence of the respondents (accused) in that case. During trial, after a lapse of about a year and 10 months Bishan Sarup had prayed on 27/8/1964 that the sample of the milk in possession of the MCD be sent to the Director, CFL. Initially the application was rejected by the Ld. Magistrate. However, the order was reviewed on 4/5/1965 and the sample was sent to the Director, CFL. On 23/4/1965 the Director had sent his report wherein he had mentioned that the fat contents of the milk were 7.2% and the non fatty solids were 6.4%. The Director, CFL also declared the sample to be adulterated. The Ld. MM took the view that "there was something infringing about 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) the report of Director, CFL because it was surprising that the Director, CFL was able to analyze the sample even after such great lapse of time". 28 The MCD preferred the appeal. However the Municipal Committee approached the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
texts.arguments: Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) also referred the statements of the DWs examined on behalf of the appellant. Counsel for the appellant has submitted that a comparison of the reports of the Public Analyst and Director CFL, would show that the two experts had found deficiencies but the reports are at variance. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kesar Devi Vs. Union of India 2003 VII AD (SC) 468 has held as under: " The judgment of a court is not to be interpreted like a statute where every word, as far as possible, has to be given a literal meaning and no word is to be ignored. The observations made have to be understood in the context of facts and contentions raised." 23 In the first instance it is the argument that in view of the law referred to above, the appellant is entitled to acquittal solely on the ground that the reports of the Public Analyst and the Director CFL were at variance exceeding .3 %. Reference on this aspect of the question may be made to the observations of the Division Bench of the Punjab High Court in Municipal Corporation of Delhi S. Nirajan Kumar and others " In such a case, as held by the Supreme Court in Ghisa Ram's case (supra) the conviction cannot be upheld on the basis of 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) the reports of the Public Analyst. But in case no prejudice is caused to the accused he cannot be allowed to escape the consequences under the law for such an anti social act which the legislature has ordained to be dealt with severely." 33 The Hon'ble High Court, in Bishan Sarup's case (supra), did not hold that since there was variance in the two reports exceeding .3% , therefore, the acquittal of the respondents was to be maintained. When the matter was considered by the Hon'ble 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) High Court in Kashi Nath's case (supra), the Hon'ble High Court had on the basis of evidence of Director CFL, who was examined as a Court Witness, the variance of .3%, as had been deposed by the Court Witness, was taken into account. The Hon'ble High court in Kashi Nath's case (supra) had taken into account the entire statement of the Director, CFL, to reach at the conclusion. The Hon'ble High court did not lay down that the moment a variation of .3% in the two reports - i.e., Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155863573/ 5 the one given by the Public Analyst and the other given by the Director CFL is found the accused has to be, with taking into account, other facts and evidence, straight away acquitted. It was not held that the variation alone irrespective of the nature of evidence, nature of the food article, nature of violation noticed by the public analyst and the prescribed standard, would be decisive. 35 In the other judgements cited by ld. Counsel for the appellant the Hon'ble High Court had, in view of the judgement rendered by the Hon'ble High Court in Kanshi Nath's case (supra), taken into account the variance between the reports of the Public Analyst and the Director CFL. 36 Use of an impermissible colour by itself, in view of rule 23 of PFA Rules, would make it a punishable offence. 40 The question as to whether the court can take into account the minor deficiencies so as to term them in the nature of permissible error was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Municipal Committee Vs. Hazara Singh (1975) 1 SCC 794. It was held that the standard fixed under the Act is one that is certain. If it is varied to any extent, the certainty of a general standard would be replaced vagaries of a fluctuating standard. Disadvantages all resulting under the predicting uncertainty and impossibility of arriving at fair and consistent decisions are great. 41 In that case a sample of milk was taken. 42 The arguments that the SLP filed by the respondent in Kanshi Nath's judgement (supra) has been dismissed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated 8/9/2011 is of no help. I would like to add that the Hon'ble Supreme Court while dismissing the criminal appeal no. 1158/07 had also observed as under: " However the question of law is kept open." The Ld. MM had Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155863573/ 6 highlighted the contradictions between the two reports and had held that the sample collected by the State was not a representative one. In that case the artificial colouring matter was also noticed. 45 In C. Mohd. Vs. State of Kerala 2007 (2) FAC 275 where in the sample of Moog Dal the Public Analyst had found .28% of Talc as foreign matter and Director CFL had found 1.363% Talc as Foreign Matter, the Hon'ble Supreme Court did not give any benefit of the variation. The conviction was upheld. 46 In Subash Vs. State 2012 (1) JCC 431 the accused was 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) convicted under 7/16 PFA Act. Our own Hon'ble High Court in para 10 of the judgement observed as under: " Keeping in view the scheme of the provisions of the Act which was intended to secure unadulterated food for the safety of the public, deviations in the prescribed standards of use of impermissible commodities in the eatables cannot be considered or termed as technical. When the legislature intended to lay down specific standards of food items, the provisions need to be given its meaning in letter and spirit and nothing could be read in between them." 47 In Hari Pada Dass Vs. State of Bengal and Anr AIR 1999 SC 1482 the argument that minor variation was likely to take place on account of natural process and it was the duty of the prosecution to establish that there was no such chance of little variation, was not accepted by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on the ground that this contention has not been raised earlier and there was no sufficient evidence on the basis of which the finding to that effect can be made. 48 Therefore, the arguments of ld. Counsel for the appellant that 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) in view of the variations in the two reports, benefit be given to the appellant, can't be accepted. 49 63 Therefore, in view of the Full Bench judgement of our own Hon'ble High Court in Bishan Sarup's case (supra) and the views taken by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in C.Mohd. Vs. State of Kerala (supra) and by our own Hon'ble High Court in Subash's case (supra) and 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) Satinder Kumar's case (supra), the argument of the appellant that in view of the variations, the appeal is liable to be accepted, is rejected.
